stem: The mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve supplies general sensation to all of the following regions EXCEPT for the:
fact: The upper lip is supplied by branches of the maxillary division, V2, rather than the mandibular division, V3.
mnemonic: V2 visits the upper lip; V3 handles the jaw and lower face.
finding: Source page displays upper lip as the exception.

stem: Regarding the vagus nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: It exits the skull through the foramen ovale.
It carries general sensation from the oropharynx.
It carries visceral afferent fibres from the aortic arch baroreceptors.
It carries parasympathetic fibres to the parotid gland.
It is the afferent nerve of the gag reflex.
fact: The vagus nerve carries visceral afferent fibres from aortic-arch baroreceptors. CN IX supplies parotid parasympathetic fibres and the afferent gag pathway.
mnemonic: X monitors the aortic arch; IX handles the parotid and gag afferent limb.
finding: Source page displays aortic-arch baroreceptor afferents as correct.

stem: The maxillary nerve supplies general sensation to all of the following regions EXCEPT for the:
fact: The maxillary division does not supply skin over the external ear; that region is supplied by other sensory nerves.
mnemonic: V2 covers the midface, palate, upper teeth, and nasal region, not the external ear.
finding: Source page displays external ear as the exception.

stem: A 45 year old lady presents to ED with right sided facial weakness. Your consultant suspects a facial nerve palsy. Which of the following clinical features would you most likely see on examination:
options: Loss of tactile sensation to anterior two-thirds of tongue
Loss of sensation to right side of face
fact: Facial-nerve palsy may cause hyperacusis because paralysis of stapedius reduces attenuation of sound.
mnemonic: VII quiets the stapes; lose VII and sounds become too loud.
finding: Source page displays hyperacusis as correct.

stem: A 56 year old female presents to ED complaining of loss of sensation over the anterior two-thirds of her tongue. Taste and salivation are intact. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected:
fact: The lingual nerve carries general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. Chorda tympani carries taste and secretomotor fibres.
mnemonic: Lingual feels; chorda tastes and stimulates saliva.
finding: Source page displays lingual nerve as correct.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is NOT typical of a facial nerve palsy:
fact: Facial palsy causes inability to close the eyelid, not inability to raise it. Eyelid elevation depends on levator palpebrae superioris via CN III and the superior tarsal muscle via sympathetic fibres.
mnemonic: VII closes the eye; III and sympathetic fibres open it.
finding: Source page displays inability to raise the eyelid as not typical.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is NOT typical for a vagal nerve palsy:
options: Uvula deviation away from the affected side
Tongue deviation towards the affected side
fact: Tongue deviation toward the affected side is a hypoglossal-nerve finding, whereas vagal palsy can cause uvula deviation, hoarseness, gag impairment, and dysphagia.
mnemonic: X affects palate and voice; XII moves the tongue.
finding: Source page displays tongue deviation towards the affected side as not typical.

stem: Regarding the glossopharyngeal nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: It is the efferent nerve of the gag reflex.
It emerges from the cranial cavity through the hypoglossal canal.
It carries taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.
It innervates the tensor veli palatini muscle.
It provides parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the parotid gland.
fact: The glossopharyngeal nerve supplies parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the parotid gland, motor fibres to stylopharyngeus, and taste from the posterior third of the tongue.
mnemonic: IX: parotid, stylopharyngeus, posterior tongue, and gag afferent.
finding: Source page displays parotid parasympathetic supply as correct.

stem: Regarding the facial nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: Forehead sparing in facial nerve palsy is indicative of a lower motor neuron lesion.
The facial nerve supplies taste to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.
The facial nerve carries parasympathetic fibres to the lacrimal glands.
The facial nerve leaves the brainstem at the cerebellopontine angle.
The facial nerve exits the skull via the stylomastoid foramen.
fact: Forehead sparing indicates an upper motor neuron lesion, not a lower motor neuron facial-nerve lesion. Peripheral facial palsy involves the forehead.
mnemonic: UMN spares the forehead; LMN takes the whole side.
finding: Source page displays forehead sparing as indicative of an LMN lesion as the incorrect statement.

stem: Which of the following nerves is the afferent pathway of the pupillary light reflex:
fact: The optic nerve carries the afferent limb of the pupillary light reflex; the oculomotor nerve carries the efferent parasympathetic limb.
mnemonic: II sees the light; III constricts the pupil.
finding: Source page displays optic nerve as correct.
